definition: PRAC (Probabilistic Action Cores) is an interpreter for natural-language instructions for robotic applications developed at the Institute for Artificial Intelligence at the University of Bremen, Germany, and is supported in parts by the European Commission and the German Research Foundation (DFG).
details: PRAC (Probabilistic Action Cores) is an interpreter for natural-language instructions for robotic applications developed at the Institute for Artificial Intelligence at the University of Bremen, Germany, and is supported in parts by the European Commission and the German Research Foundation (DFG).

explainer.lead: PRAC (Probabilistic Action Cores) is an interpreter that turns natural-language instructions into robot actions. It matters because it bridges how people speak and how robots execute tasks.

tiers.eli5: You tell a robot in plain words what to do, and PRAC works out the steps it needs to take.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to map free-text commands onto robotic action representations rather than hand-coding every instruction. A pitfall is that instruction wording varies widely, so interpretation must handle ambiguity robustly.
tiers.paperLevel: PRAC is an interpreter for natural-language instructions for robotic applications, developed at the Institute for Artificial Intelligence at the University of Bremen, Germany, supported in parts by the European Commission and the German Research Foundation (DFG).

explainer.example: A user's spoken or written instruction is parsed by PRAC into an action core a robot can execute, rather than requiring a fixed command syntax.
